Shri B.K. Upadhyay - Government Advocate for respondent No.
 Order

By the instant petition filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the petitioners are claiming following relief:-
"It is therefore, prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to call for the case diary of Crime No.887/2015 from Police Station Kolgawan, District Satna, for its kind perusal and after perusal of the case diary may kindly be pleased to quash the registration of Crime No.887/2015 at Police Station Kolgawan, District Satna for the offences under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code registered against the petitioners in the interest of justice."
2.

During the pendency of this petition, a revision has been filed by the present petitioners i.e.
Criminal Revision No.5540 of 2023 under Section 397 r/w Section 401 of Cr.P.C. seeking quashing of order dated 11.09.2023 whereby the trial Court exercising the power provided under Section 228 of Cr.P.C. has framed charges in S.T. No.27/2023 under Sections 420, 467, 468, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12757 2 MCRC-62340-2021 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code against the present petitioners and that revision is connected with the instant case and both the cases are being decided simultaneously.

sentences.text: As per the facts of the case, the present petitioners are permanent residents of Satna District, they are agriculturists and working as education extension officers.
They are also the Directors of VIP Campion School, Gram Badkhar, District Satna, Madhya Pradesh.
A recognition was granted to the school on the basis of title over the land where the school was situated after fulfilling other requirements.

4. A complaint was made by one Kamlesh Tripathi to the District Panchayat Officer saying that the present petitioners have no title over the land and by preparing forged documents, they have obtained recognition from the competent authority for running the school.

On the basis of said complaint, the District Panchayat Officer has directed an inquiry and the Sub Divisional Officer (Revnue), Raghuraj Nagar, conducted an inquiry and gave opinion that the recognition for running the school was obtained by the petitioners on the basis of forged documents.

Thereafter, respondent No.2, wrote a letter to the Station House Officer, Police Station Kolgawan, District Satna, on 21.09.2015 and on the basis of said letter, an FIR got registered against the present petitioners under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC vide Crime No.887/2015 and thereafter the charge-sheet was filed and the trial Court vide order dated 11.09.2023 has framed the charges against the present petitioners.
5.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that registration of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:12757 3 MCRC-62340-2021 FIR and initiation of criminal proceeding is absolutely illegal and misuse of process of law.

He has submitted that the intension of the private respondent and the complainant was nothing but to grab the land of the present petitioners and as such, after making a plan, a complaint was made and inquiry was conducted, in which, without any authority, it has been ascertained that the present petitioners have no title over the land and the recognition obtained by them on the basis of forged documents of title.

He has further submitted that the present petitioners have sought for quashing of FIR and also the criminal proceedings on the ground that it is nothing but an abuse of process of law and the prosecution is malicious because according to them, the Sub Divisional Officer (Revenue) conducted the inquiry holding that the present petitioners have no title over the land whereas this cannot be ascertained by the SDO and if at all it got done, at the most, the recognition granted in favour of the present petitioners could have been cancelled by the authority granting recognition, but registration of FIR without any foundation is not proper.

He has submitted that the Project Officer, who wrote a letter to the Station House Officer has no authority to determine the said fact without seeking any declaration from the competent authority or Court having jurisdiction to make such declaration.

He has further submitted that it is nothing but a plan made by the complainant with an intension to grab the land of the present petitioners and, therefore, the present petitioners have been falsely implicated in the alleged offence so as to face harassment and to accept the conditions of the complainant and other persons who were intending to get the land transferred in their favour.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12757 4 MCRC-62340-2021 6.

The counsel for the State has opposed the submissions made by the counsel for the petitioners and submitted that it is a fraud committed by the present petitioners and, therefore, registration of FIR cannot be said to be illegal in any manner.

sentences.text: However, I am not convinced with the submission made by the counsel for the State and even after perusal of record, it is something surprising that the Project Officer without any authority has written a letter to the Station House Officer, Police Station Kolgawan, District Satna, for registration of offence.

It is a private land and if title was not there and any illegality was committed while taking recognition, the said authority can be directed to make an inquiry and then recognition could have been cancelled but registration of FIR that too by the authority i.e. the Project Officer is not proper.

He has no authority to get the offence registered that too only on the basis of complaint made by a private person alleging against the present petitioners questioning their title over the land where the school was being run.
8. The Sub Divisional Officer has no authority to hold in its report that the present petitioners have no title over the land.
Under such circumstances, I am of the opinion that the whole prosecution is malicious and initiated by the authority not competent to do so.

It is not a case in which it is alleged that the present petitioners have played a fraud with the Government and claimed their title over the Government land but it is a case in which it is alleged that the recognition for running the school has been obtained by placing the documents of title in regard to the land for which they did not have title.

The NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12757 5 MCRC-62340-2021 authority which has granted recognition at the most could cancel the recognition observing that the same was wrongly granted but no prosecution could have been initiated at the instance of Project Officer that too on a complaint made by a private person.

9. After perusal of case diary, it reflects that a complaint was made by one private person alleging that the VIP Campion School Badkhar has been granted recognition on the basis of forged and fabricated documents.

The- then Director of the school has obtained the said recognition and various authorities were involved therein and, therefore, an inquiry on the basis of complaint made by one Kamlesh Tripathi was initiated by the-then Sub Divisional Officer, Raghuraj Nagar, District Satna, and he submitted a report on 19.05.2015 before the Chief Executive Officer, Zila Panchayat,
Satna, in which it is opined that the land over which the school is situated belongs to one Kamlesh Tripathi S/o Laxmi Prasad Tripathi.
It is also opined that the recognition has been granted on the basis of documents submitted by the- then Director of the school.

Thereafter, the Project Officer on 15.09.2015, has issued a letter to the Station House Officer for initiating criminal prosecution and on the basis of same, an FIR got registered vide Crime No.887/2015 at Police Station Kolgawan,
District Satna.
10.

It is something surprising as to how the Project Officer without any permission from the higher authorities initiated criminal prosecution against the government officers presently posted and retired.
From the record, nowhere it reveals that even the permission from the Collector has been taken to initiate prosecution.

If this practice is approved, then it may NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:12757 6 MCRC-62340-2021 create a chaos that any government employee can write a letter to the police officer so as to initiate criminal prosecution against any other officer or employee of the government.
This practice is not prevailing and even not acceptable.

At the most, if it is found that the recognition was not properly granted, the authority can initiate proceeding giving opportunity of hearing to the school concerned so as to substantiate whether recognition was proper or not.

If it is found that the recognition was wrongly granted, the same could have been cancelled Ashok Kumar Mishra @ Dipak Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153655496/

sentences.text: 3 but one sided action initiating criminal prosecution only on the basis of letter of one government employee is not proper.

11. After perusal of record, this Court finds that the land over which the school is being run belongs to a private person and there was some dispute in respect of the said land and one party made a complaint to the authority about the recognition granted to the school situated over the land and the inquiry conducted one sided without giving any opportunity of hearing and only on the basis of a report of SDO, the Project Officer wrote a letter to the SHO, in pursuance to which the FIR got registered and the charge-sheet was filed.

This type of prosecution is not acceptable and cannot be approved and as per the allegations made by the counsel for the petitioners, it is a malicious prosecution and in fact, it is a plan to harass the present petitioners only to grab their land by some of the persons including some government officers.

The trial Court has also not examined this aspect and without applying its mind, registered the offence and also framed charges against the present petitioners and that order of framing of charges is also under challenge.

In the facts situation,
registration of offence vide Crime NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12757 7 MCRC-62340-2021 No.887/2015 is not sustainable in the eyes of law.

12. The Supreme Court in case of State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal & Others reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 , has laid down the yardsticks for quashing of FIR exercising the power provided under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraphs i.e. 102 and 103 are as under:-
"102.

In the backdrop of the interpretation of the various relevant provisions of the Code under Chapter XIV and of the principles of law enunciated by this Court in a series of decisions relating to the exercise of the extraordinary power under Article 226 or the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code which we have extracted and reproduced above, we give the following categories of cases by way of illustration wherein such power could be exercised either to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice, though it may not be possible to lay down any precise, clearly defined and sufficiently channelised and inflexible guidelines or rigid formulate and to give an exhaustive list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power should be exercised: (1) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.

(2) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any, accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence,
justifying an investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.

(3)
Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused. (4) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under Section 155(2) of the Code.

(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which Ashok Kumar Mishra @ Dipak Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153655496/
4

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

(6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the Act concerned (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the Act concerned, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

(7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge.

103. We also give a note of caution to the effect that the power of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12757 8 MCRC-62340-2021 quashing a criminal proceeding should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in the rarest of rare cases; that the court will not be justified in embarking upon an enquiry as to the reliability or genuineness or otherwise of the allegations made in the FIR or the complaint and that the extraordinary or inherent powers do not confer an arbitrary jurisdiction on the court to act according to its whim or caprice."

13. Thus, in view of the aforesaid, it is clear that it is a fit case in which this Court can exercise the power provided under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. because the prosecution initiated against the present petitioners and other officers by the department is not proper and that is completely mala fide action on the part of the authority and such a prosecution is not sustainable in the eyes of law, ergo,
it is hereby set aside.
The FIR registered against the present petitioners vide Crime No.887/2015 at Police Station Kolgawan, District Santa, is hereby set aside.
The petition is allowed and disposed of.

1 4 . Ex consequentia, the connected petition i.e. Criminal Revision No.5540 of 2023 and the order impugned therein dated 11.09.2023 passed by the trial Court in S.T. No.27/2023 framing charges against the present petitioners is also not sustainable.
Accordingly, the same is also set aside.

Criminal Revision No.5540 of 2023 is also allowed and disposed of.
15.
All the proceedings initiated against the present petitioners in pursuance of the offence registered vide Crime No.887/2015 shall stand quashed.
(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12757 9 MCRC-62340-2021 ac/-
